note: Preserved workflow tasks moved out of the product feature tree.

tasks.title: Integration authority
tasks.text: Local integration after checks is approved; the owner authorized the first local commits only, while later commits, pushes, tags, releases, deployment and publication still need approval.

tasks.title: Task ownership
tasks.text: Claim one ready leaf with baseline, allowed files, dependency evidence and budget. The coordinator owns claims and shared files. Separate workers cannot concurrently edit the same file.

tasks.title: Independent review
tasks.text: Use a separate reviewer for changed semantics, lifetime and concurrency. Add a second reviewer for numerical guarantees, unsafe interfaces or cross-backend changes. Review findings require reproductions or concrete reasoning, not stylistic expansion.

tasks.title: Blocker handling
tasks.text: After two materially different failed approaches, or the task budget, record the smallest reproducer and stop that task. Do not weaken a guarantee to unblock it. The coordinator reassigns independent work; a missing device, dependency, decision and defect have different owners.

tasks.title: Local integration
tasks.text: Verify the baseline and apply only owned changes. Resolve shared-file edits through the coordinator. Run focused checks plus affected integration; retain failures and a reversible patch. No stash, hard reset or destructive cleanup of shared work.

tasks.title: Trial round
tasks.text: Start with three disjoint tasks and one integrator/reviewer. Measure elapsed time, conflict rate and escaped defects before increasing concurrency. Worker count is bounded by ready tasks, file ownership, hardware capacity and budget.

tasks.title: Start with a small acceptance slice
tasks.text: Before implementation, write the contract and the smallest failing public-behavior examples. For a routine feature, start with a normal case, a boundary and an explained failure; high-risk synchronization needs its safety case immediately.

children.title: Choose the oracle
children.text: Use a specification, independent arithmetic/model or independently implemented reference. Never generate expected answers from the implementation under test.

children.title: Verify the failure
children.text: Show that the test fails for the missing behavior, not an import mistake or broken fixture.

children.title: Bound the first round
children.text: Avoid exhaustive matrices, broad mocks and fixture frameworks before a working vertical slice. Expand early only when a real risk or failure demands it.

children.title: Independent expectation
children.text: Write expectations before copying implementation logic. One normal case, one relevant boundary and one failure are a starting heuristic, not a quota. Expand around semantics, not line counts.

tasks.title: Implement and refactor
tasks.text: Make the acceptance slice pass; run the nearest existing tests. Keep the public API and oracle stable while refactoring internals. Do not repeatedly run the full suite after every edit.

tasks.title: Expand after the slice works
tasks.text: Before integration, add the missing behavior classes and target coverage justified by the feature.

children.title: Hypothesis properties
children.text: Generate valid shapes/dtypes/strides directly. Separate finite arithmetic, special-value cases and invalid inputs. A floating-point identity is a property only under the declared contract.

children.title: Fault sensitivity
children.text: For important tests, show they catch a representative wrong implementation: wrong denominator, dropped lane, sign/rounding change or premature resource release. Use targeted mutation checks, not a mandatory full mutation campaign.

children.title: Independent review
children.text: Review whether assertions establish the requested behavior. Coverage can reveal gaps; it does not prove semantic correctness. Do not discard a valid failing test just because the current code fails it.

tasks.title: Budget test execution
tasks.text: Use a fast local profile, broader integration profile and bounded scheduled campaign; measure suite cost before setting limits.

children.title: Preserve counterexamples
children.text: Persist Hypothesis examples where useful, then promote important shrunk failures to explicit regression cases. Record Hypothesis version and inputs; a seed alone is not a durable cross-version replay.

children.title: Separate generation from launches
children.text: Generate many cheap model cases; replay a representative corpus on devices. Amortize compilation by specialization, not by changing numerical policy.

children.title: Reset state per example
children.text: A pytest function-scoped fixture is not recreated for each Hypothesis example. Reset streams, buffers, warnings and global settings inside each generated case.

children.title: Separate deadlines from benchmarks
children.text: For selected asynchronous/JIT tests, disable Hypothesis’s per-example deadline only with an outer test/job timeout. max_examples is not a hard cap on all shrink/replay work.

children.title: Lifecycle state machines
children.text: Use rule-based stateful tests for allocate/launch/await/cancel/drain/release and graph/cache ownership; check invariants after each transition.

tasks.code:
# Illustrative profiles; calibrate counts against measured suite cost.
from hypothesis import settings

settings.register_profile("local", max_examples=20)
settings.register_profile("integration", max_examples=100)
# Keep shrinking/replay enabled. Bound the enclosing job separately.

tasks.title: Test real integration
tasks.text: Keep one thin public path from installed package through capture, compiler, launch and result. Mocks test failure handling; they do not certify hardware.

children.title: Installed artifact
children.text: Build a wheel and test it outside the checkout with CPU-only and selected extras. Verify JIT compiler diagnostics and package contents.

children.title: GPU scheduling
children.text: Parallelize isolated CPU tests. Serialize tests sharing device/global state; reserve exclusive GPU access for timing and use separate concurrency tests.

children.title: Failure accounting
children.text: Use strict expected failures with a cause and completion task. Missing required hardware fails that runner’s job; optional absent hardware is reported as unavailable, never passed.

children.title: Sanitizer pass
children.text: Run selected memory/synchronization kernels under vendor tools. NVIDIA memcheck/racecheck/synccheck cover different hazards; a clean run is not a proof of every race.
